_about: Traffic assumptions, read by the k6 tests and the analyser.

_labels._about: Short labels for the dashboard's assumptions (unit after the value). Keys without a label aren't shown there.

_expected_peak_visitors: Visitors on the site at once during a normal busy hour.
_campaign_peak_visitors: Visitors on the site at once just after an ad goes live.
_avg_visit_seconds: How long one visit lasts. null = measure it from the run's healthy stages (before the knee).
_planning_visit_seconds: Estimated visit length, used only to turn the peaks into k6 arrival rates before a run (visitors at once / visit length = visits per second). The analyser measures the real length afterwards.
_patience_seconds: Assumption: how long a visitor waits for a page or a form before leaving. Applies to requests the visitor waits for (see on_failure in analyzer/route-context.json); k6 uses this or the site's own timeout, whichever is shorter.
_dataset_rows: Rows in the main table (users) during the tests: the seed size. Used to estimate how slow lookups would get as the table grows.

main_funnel._about: load-tests/main.js: every visitor lands on / and loads /api/rates, then some go on to sign up. The shares are the same at every load level, so only traffic volume changes between stages.
main_funnel._go_to_signup: Assumption: share of visitors who click through from / to /signup.
main_funnel._submit_signup: Assumption: share of those who submit the form. The rest leave (voluntary drop-off).
main_funnel._reuse_seeded_email: Share of submissions using an existing email, to hit the 'already taken' path.

signup_test._about: load-tests/signup.js: visitors land directly on /signup, like an ad campaign that links straight to sign-up. They skip the homepage and rates, so rates can't hide the sign-up problems.
signup_test._scenario: Every visitor lands straight on /signup, which only happens during a sign-up ad campaign. On a normal day about 30% of visitors reach sign-up (the main test), so the analyser judges this test at the campaign peak, and takes normal-day sign-up numbers from the latest main run.
